title: Digital Document Validity (DigiLocker / mParivahan)
summary: Police cannot compel production of physical documents if presented via DigiLocker or mParivahan.
key_provisions: Driving Licence, Registration Certificate (RC), Insurance Certificate, and PUC presented electronically in DigiLocker or mParivahan are legally equivalent to physical original documents under Section 4 of the Information Technology Act 2000 and Rule 139 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.
Law enforcement authorities have direct access to the mParivahan and Sarathi databases to verify electronic records; motorists cannot be penalized solely for not carrying laminated cards.
In situations where an offence requires impoundment or licence suspension, the seizure is recorded electronically on the eChallan portal without confiscating the physical card.

title: 15-Day Document Production Grace Period
statutory_basis: Section 130 Motor Vehicles Act 1988 & Rule 139 CMVR
summary: Motorists have 15 days to present vehicle documents if not immediately available at the time of inspection.
key_provisions: If a motorist cannot produce documents immediately upon demand by a police officer in uniform, they cannot be instantly convicted if they undertake to produce them within 15 days.
Documents (Licence, RC, Certificate of Insurance) can be produced within 15 days at the designated police station or office of the enforcement authority.
The statutory penalty for failure to carry documents does not apply if valid documents are produced within this statutory window.

title: Virtual Courts Online Challan Disposal
statutory_basis: e-Courts Project, Supreme Court of India & Ministry of Law and Justice
summary: Non-compoundable and contested challans can be adjudicated and paid online via Virtual Courts without visiting a physical courtroom.
key_provisions: Motorists who receive a court-referred challan notice can access https://vcourts.gov.in to review proceedings without physical attendance.
The virtual judge examines the challan; the citizen can plead guilty and pay the judicially assessed fine online, or contest the challan to transfer it to a regular open court.

title: Official e-Challan Grievance & Wrong Challan Dispute
summary: Dispute incorrect challans (e.g. cloned number plate, wrong vehicle detected) directly on the official Parivahan portal.
key_provisions: If an e-challan has been issued incorrectly due to automated camera OCR errors, mismatched plates, or vehicle theft, motorists can lodge an official grievance at https://echallan.parivahan.gov.in/gsticket/.
Provide the challan number, vehicle registration number, and photographic evidence to request review before the challan is forwarded to court.

title: National Emergency & Roadside Assistance Helplines
statutory_basis: Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) & NHAI Guidelines
summary: Key toll-free emergency helplines accessible 24/7 across India.
key_provisions: 112 — National Emergency Response Support System (Police, Fire, Medical, integrated emergency response).
1033 — National Highway Emergency & Assistance (Toll-free 24/7 ambulance, patrol, and breakdown assistance on all National Highways).
